newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-MAGIC HIRE CHUCK DALY AS HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-MAGIC HIRE CHUCK DALY AS HEAD COACH.

text.p: Hall-of-Famer Chuck Daly was named on Tuesday as the new head coach of the Orlando Magic.

Daly, best known for leading the Detroit Pistons to back-to-back NBA titles in 1988 and 1989 and in steering the original Dream Team to 1992 Olympic gold in Barcelona, signed a deal worth a reported $15 million over three years.
"I've never disguised the fact that you're only as good as the players who perform for you," said the 66-year-old Daly, who gets one of the league's best in guard Penny Hardaway.

"You only win with talent. But someone has to drive the bus and I've learned over the years how to manoeuvre in that situation. I am basically a teacher and a basketball coach. That's what I do, that's what I am."
Daly has not coached since he left the New Jersey Nets after the 1993-94 season. He has been working since as an analyst on NBA telecasts.

Orlando president and general manager John Gabriel said: "We're ecstatic to be able to bring a coach of Chuck Daly's status here to such a young organisation. We're bringing in one of the greatest coaches in the history of the game."
"He coached 11 consecutive playoff teams, he ranks fifth all-time in playoff history winning percentage and was selected to be first coach of the Dream Team," Gabriel added.
Daly added a familiar name to his staff, naming Brendan Suhr an assistant.
Another Hall-of-Famer, former Philadelphia 76ers star Julius Erving, is reported to be ready to join the organisation's front office.

Orlando fired Brian Hill in midseason and named assistant Richie Adubato as his replacement. The Magic finished 45-37 and lost to the second-seeded Miami Heat, three games to two, in the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
